description: The narrowed roles of the producer backend (INFRA-050; D-S57 item 1, D-S56 item 1, D-S62 item 3), read by scripts/producer_questions.py. Each role answers one narrow question per unit or passage Python selects. A judgement is a choice decided from the model's own probabilities in one forward pass (choice_decision.py): the model writes no text, and the quote is Python's echo of the evidence it selected. A span is kept only when Python finds it verbatim in the unit. Nothing here is used until its form is decision and, for a choice, config/semantic_thresholds.json holds its family's measured threshold; until then each role runs as shipped (form reply) and the run records why. Adopting a form is a recorded decision after its measurement. No question here has been measured on a model.
unit_evidence: A unit is one of pairing_map.split_units' units of the document under review (its heading and its own text). The preamble unit counts as one. Nothing else reaches a question: no neighbour, no registry, no bus, no other document's text unless the question names it.

claim_support.evidence: one unit's own text and the one context passage pipeline._provision_aware_context_refs ranks first for it (its REF-* and text); a unit with no ranked passage is not asked

decision.template:
A part of a document and a passage from the reference material follow.

PART
{unit}

PASSAGE
{passage}

Judge only from these two texts. Does the passage support what the part states?

Answer with one word.
Yes: the passage supports what the part states.
Partly: the passage supports only some of it, or only weakly.
No: the passage bears on the part and does not support it.
Unrelated: the passage does not bear on what the part states.
decision.record_note: A settled answer writes one LEGAL_ANALYST item: claim_id the unit's id, verdict the answer's label, passage_ref the passage's REF-*, support_probabilities the decision's probabilities, quote the passage's text (Python's echo), reasoning Python's sentence naming the decision and its probability, ref_ids [passage_ref]. An unsettled answer writes none and is counted. Every item is a model's (written_by model), summary-only and never promoted.

speech_act.evidence: one line of one unit (a line carrying a letter or a digit, the unit's heading line excepted), at most max_lines_per_unit lines a unit, in order

decision.answers_note: OPERATOR-DECLARED: the acts are the operator's own words, given here as {label, surface, meaning}; none is in code. With no act declared the question is never asked, whatever the form, and the run records why. Unclear (cannot be settled) is always added by Python.

citation_target.evidence: one line of one unit that names, by the shared tokeniser (pairing_map._norm_label), every word of the name of at least one OTHER document of the corpus, and the names of those documents
citation_target.python_first: A line naming exactly one other document resolves to it by Python with no call (resolved true, decided_by python). A line naming two to max_candidates documents is asked. More than max_candidates is refused and counted. A line naming none is not a citation by this test.

decision.answers_note: A question offers only the letters of its own candidates and None; Unclear is added by Python.
decision.record_note: A settled letter writes one CITATION_RESOLVER item: source_document the document under review, target_document the candidate's name, citation_form the line (Python's echo), resolved true. None writes resolved false. Unsettled writes none and is counted.

extraction.keep: an item is kept only when its name and its evidence_in_text are each found verbatim in the unit (whitespace-normalised); otherwise it is refused with its reason and counted

an element is kept only when its name is found verbatim in the unit (whitespace-normalised); document_count and document_names are computed by Python over the corpus (the documents whose text holds the name verbatim), never the model's; title, date and chronology are left to Python's dating rule, which refuses rather than guesses

editorial_verdict.evidence: one observation: the finding's own sentence and the text of the unit it concerns
editorial_verdict.routing: An observation on a model's finding goes to a rank whose backend is in the other model family from the backend of the bus post that carried the finding (finding_record.written_by). A Python finding may go to either family. With no rank of the other family in the run, no model reviews it and the record says so.

decision.template:
A finding about a part of a document and the part follow.

FINDING
{finding}

PART
{unit}

Judge only from these two texts. Is the finding sound?

Answer with one word.
Sound: the part bears the finding out.
Concern: the finding may be wrong or overstated.
Serious: the part contradicts the finding.
decision.record_note: A settled answer writes one item for the rank: ref the finding's REF-*, verdict the label, rationale Python's sentence naming the decision and its probability, quote the finding's sentence (Python's echo). Unsettled writes none and is counted.
